sweep_summary: Both works with stress in the title are duplicate Glottolog records of one work, Hildebrandt 2005 (LTBA 28.1), which is already held (image-only scan + scanned) and was re-read: its suprasegmental section is entirely about word tone and it is silent on stress placement except one incidental 'unstressed (second) syllable' remark on p. 15, consistent with the catalog's root-initial coding. The catalog's deciding passage (Hildebrandt 2004, §2.6, pp. 37-39) was re-verified verbatim in the text we hold layer and stays the best first-hand statement; nothing read supersedes it. One new, weaker datum: the AUTOTYP Word Domains database (Bickel, Hildebrandt & Schiering; refetched from GitHub) codes Manange as 'Exactly 1 Main Stress, Penult' over 'stem ± prefix ± suffix ± particle' from 'Grammar Explicit' evidence, a label that diverges from 'root-initial' whenever a root is polysyllabic or prefixed; this is a secondary coding and merits a note, not a reclassification. Unread candidates worth acquiring: Hildebrandt & Anderson 2023 'Word Prominence in Languages of Southern Asia' (OUP, high), Hildebrandt 2015 'The Prosodic Word' (OUP handbook, medium), Bickel, Hildebrandt & Schiering 2009 (De Gruyter, medium; source of the AUTOTYP coding), Hildebrandt 2013/2018 CUP sketch (low). sealang.net unreachable; DOI landing for the LTBA paper (dr.ntu.edu.sg) behind an AWS WAF captcha; OUP/Cambridge pages show no abstract.

tone_statements.quote: Each monosyllabic word, in languages of the TGTM group, can carry one of four tones. ... [§3.12 table, column MANANGBA Ngawal:] tone-1 33 tone-2 45 tone-3 54 tone-4 31 ... [§3.21] In Manangba the system is even more different. There is no use of breathy vs. clear voice quality, but rather a normal voice for the two lower tones and a very tense quality for the two high tones. The two higher tones here are not /1/ and /2/ as expected, but /3/ and /2/. Tone-1 is lower-mid level, and tone-4 is a fall from mid to low.

tone_statements.summary: Four word-tones (all TGTM); Ngawal Manangba 33, 45, 54, 31. Manangba: no breathy/clear split, tense voice on the two high tones (/3/, /2/); tone-1 lower-mid level, tone-4 mid-to-low fall. Suffixes toneless, root tone spreads over the word. Intro calls TGTM 'marginally tonal'. Nothing on stress.
